# StatusBadge

```tsx
import { StatusBadge } from '@harnessio/ui/components'
```

Status: `beta`. Sources: [manifest](../../src/components/status-badge/status-badge.manifest.json), [guide](../../src/components/status-badge/status-badge.guide.md).

Visual indicator for a transient, system-driven state. Uses a closed, evaluative semantic palette (muted/success/warning/danger/info/merged/risk), never an open categorical one. See status-badge.guide.md SBD-001/002 for when to choose StatusBadge vs Tag.

## Use when

- Value is a state that changes automatically (pending → active → closed).
- Color implies judgment (good/bad/neutral/waiting).
- Exactly one status per object (mutually exclusive).
- Status can change while visible; caller wraps with aria-live=polite.

## Do not use when

- Value is a stable attribute describing what a thing is — use Tag instead.
- Multiple statuses apply to the same object — use separate badges or Tag.
- Badge needs to be interactive — use Tag's interactive props.
- Need open/uncontrolled color palette — use Tag's 15-color palette.
- Need to combine two statuses (e.g. 'Error, Pending') — pick one or render separately.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
| ---- | ---- | -------- | ------- | ----- |
| `variant` | `primary` \| `secondary` \| `outline` \| `ghost` \| `status` | yes |  | Required by StatusBadgeProps. cva defaultVariants still sets 'primary' when an untyped caller omits it. |
| `theme` | `muted` \| `success` \| `warning` \| `danger` \| `info` \| `merged` \| `risk` | no | `"muted"` |  |
| `size` | `sm` \| `md` | no | `"md"` |  |
| `icon` | `string` | no | `null` | never on variant='status'; optional on others Typed as keyof typeof IconNameMapV2 (an icon name), not a free string. |
| `children` | `node` | yes |  |  |
| `pulse` | `boolean` | no |  | only when variant='status' Renders animate-pulse on the indicator dot. No Figma property. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  | Style override escape hatch via cn(). |

Figma-only properties, with no code prop: `state`.

## Constraints

- When `variant` is `status`: do not pass `icon`. (SBD-007, enforced by types)
- When `variant` is `primary` or `secondary` or `outline` or `ghost`: do not pass `pulse`. (SBD-007, enforced by types)

## Illegal combinations

- `variant` is `ghost` or `status` and `state` is `hover` (figma): Figma node 1293:5995 has 112 of 140 possible variants. The 28 missing are every ghost and status variant with state=hover.

## Do's and Do Not's

### Do's

- Use StatusBadge for _transient, system-driven state_ that changes automatically (pending → active → closed).
- Pass `children` text always — text is mandatory and conveys all semantic meaning.
- Wrap with `aria-live="polite"` when status can change while visible (connectivity, job progress, etc.).
- Default to `outline` variant absent a specific reason to pick `primary`, `secondary`, `ghost`, or `status`.
- Use the fixed icon table (check-circle/xmark-circle/timer/pause/prohibition/warning-circle) for Pass/Fail/Pending meanings across any domain.
- Render one StatusBadge per object — pick the most urgent status if multiple apply.

### Do Not's

- Don't use for stable _attributes_ describing what a thing is (account tier, scope, marketing labels) — use Tag instead.
- Don't pass `icon` when `variant='status'` — the indicator dot already occupies that slot.
- Don't pass `pulse` on variants other than `'status'` — pulse only works with the status variant.
- [TK: draft for Katie] Don't recreate pulse with `className` (for example `animate-pulse` or `motion-safe:animate-pulse`) on any variant. A badge gets an icon or a pulse, never both; if it needs to pulse, use `variant='status'` with `pulse` and drop the icon. Incorrect: `<StatusBadge variant="outline" theme="success" icon="check-circle" className="motion-safe:animate-pulse">Running</StatusBadge>`. (SBD-007)
- Don't stack multiple StatusBadges to represent simultaneous statuses — pick the most urgent or render separate badges.
- Don't rely on color or icon alone to convey meaning — text is mandatory.
- Don't add `role`, `tabIndex`, `onClick`, or `aria-readonly` at the call site — they're explicitly stripped from props. StatusBadge is non-interactive by design.
- Don't use `info`, `merged`, or `risk` themes for generic Pass/Fail/Pending indicators — restrict to `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `muted`. Reserve `info`/`merged`/`risk` for named, non-execution exceptions (e.g., "Merged" PR badge).

## Accessibility

Keyboard support: none.

Non-interactive by design: role, aria-readonly, tabIndex, onClick and color are omitted from props. All semantic meaning lives in children text. No built-in aria-live; callers must wrap with aria-live=polite for live-changing status. See SBD-008 in status-badge.guide.md.

### SBD-001 — StatusBadge represents state, Tag represents attribute

Checked by: `review`.

`StatusBadge` is for something that _changes_ — usually system- or backend-driven, transient, and evaluative (the color implies good/bad/waiting). `Tag` is for something that _describes what a thing is_ — stable, descriptive, no implied judgment, and open/categorical rather than a closed semantic palette. These are two different components with two different prop contracts; neither should absorb the other's job via a `type` prop.

### SBD-002 — Decision test for choosing StatusBadge over Tag

Checked by: `review`.

Ask: _does this value change automatically as a result of a system process, and does the color choice imply something is good/bad/waiting?_ Yes → `StatusBadge`. No — even if it visually mimics badge styling — → `Tag`.

### SBD-003 — Ambiguous cases (tier, scope, marketing labels, connectivity) need per-case judgment, not a default

Checked by: `review`.

Some values don't resolve cleanly from SBD-002 and have been called out explicitly rather than forced into either bucket:

- **Account type/tier** (Free/Pro/Enterprise) — a ranked category. Treat as `Tag`, though it can borrow badge-like visual weight; consider a distinct "plan chip" variant if this recurs.
- **Scope** (Public/Private/Internal) — not evaluative, but affects what a user can do. Best as `Tag` with an icon (lock/globe), not color-coded like a status.
- **Marketing labels** ("Beta", "New") — informational `Tag`s; no lifecycle within the object's own state machine.
- **Connectivity** (online/offline/reconnecting) — IS a `StatusBadge`: system-driven, evaluative, mutually exclusive, real lifecycle transitions. Usually needs an `aria-live` wrapper (see SBD-008) since it can change while the user is looking at the screen.

### SBD-004 — StatusBadge is an indicator, not a button

Checked by: `types:StatusBadgeProps`, `test:packages/ui/src/components/status-badge/__tests__/status-badge.rules.test.tsx#SBD-004 renders a non-interactive indicator`.

Universal design-system rule, not specific to this component: a badge signals state, it doesn't take action. `status-badge.tsx` enforces this at the type level — `role`, `aria-readonly`, `tabIndex`, `onClick`, and `color` are explicitly `Omit<>`'d from the prop type, so a consumer cannot wire click/focus behavior onto it even by accident. If a status needs to be clickable or filterable, that is a different, interactive component (e.g. `Tag`'s `onActionClick`/`enableHover`), not an augmented `StatusBadge`.

Figma defines `state=hover` variants for `primary`, `secondary` and `outline`. Code has no hover styles. This conflicts with the rule above and is listed in the manifest's `knownGaps`.

### SBD-005 — One StatusBadge per object — no stacking multiple statuses

Checked by: `review`.

Don't combine multiple statuses into one badge (e.g. "Error, Pending"). If an item genuinely has more than one simultaneous state, pick the single most urgent one, or render separate badges with clear spacing rules — never two states inside one badge.

### SBD-006 — Text label is mandatory; color and icon never carry meaning alone

Checked by: `test:packages/ui/src/components/status-badge/__tests__/status-badge.rules.test.tsx#SBD-006 exposes only the text label to assistive tech`, `review`.

The manifest marks `children` as required with no default, so a `StatusBadge` must not be rendered icon-only or color-only. Color-only and icon-only signals fail colorblind users and grayscale contexts (printouts, screenshots); icon may reinforce meaning but never solely carries it.

The type does not enforce this yet: `StatusBadgeProps` inherits an optional `children` from `React.HTMLAttributes`. The manifest's `knownGaps` waives that mismatch until the type or a test enforces it.

### SBD-007 — icon and pulse are mutually exclusive by variant

Checked by: `types:StatusBadgeProps`, `schema:/constraints`, `test:packages/ui/src/components/status-badge/__tests__/status-badge.rules.test.tsx#SBD-007 gives the status variant the indicator and pulse, and other variants the icon`, `lint:no-restricted-syntax`.

`StatusBadgeProps` is a discriminated union: when `variant="status"`, `icon` is typed `never` (the status variant already owns the indicator-dot slot) and `pulse?: boolean` is available. For every other variant, `pulse` is typed `never` and `icon` is available. An agent should never try to pass both on the same instance — the type system already blocks it, but a design-side agent generating usage examples needs to know why. The manifest's `constraints` list encodes the same rule for tools that do not run the type checker.

### SBD-008 — Known gap: no built-in aria-live — consumers must wrap live-changing statuses themselves

Checked by: `review`.

Consumers must apply `aria-live="polite"` at the call site when status can change while visible (connectivity, job progress). The component itself cannot handle this.

### SBD-009 — Fixed shape and a 2-size scale, system-wide — never vary shape by meaning

Checked by: `types:StatusBadgeProps`, `review`.

One shape (rounded-rect), two sizes (`sm`/`md`). Never vary shape by meaning or introduce a third size.

### SBD-010 — theme is a closed semantic enum — never an ad hoc per-team color

Checked by: `types:StatusBadgeProps`, `schema:/props/shared/1/values`, `test:packages/ui/src/components/status-badge/__tests__/status-badge.rules.test.tsx#SBD-010 maps every manifest theme to its semantic class and accepts no others`.

`theme` values: `muted | success | warning | danger | info | merged | risk`. Don't invent ad hoc theme values per team or surface.

### SBD-014 — Pipeline execution status badges use only 4 of the 7 themes — success, warning, muted, danger

Checked by: `review`.

Don't use `info`, `merged`, `risk` for execution status. Icon table (check/xmark/timer/pause/prohibition/warning-circle) is unratified; icon-to-substate pairing is still proposed.

### SBD-015 — Tree View owns inline execution-status rendering in hierarchical lists — don't hand-compose StatusBadge

Checked by: `review`.

In hierarchical lists (steps within stage, stages within pipeline), use Tree View's built-in rendering instead of hand-composing StatusBadge + icon.

### SBD-016 — Guidance: reach for the outline variant absent a specific reason to choose another

Checked by: `review`.

Consumer guidance: `outline` is lowest visual weight and reads neutral by default. Pick `primary`, `secondary`, `ghost`, or `status` only with deliberate intent.

### SBD-017 — Reuse pipeline status icons for any Pass/Fail/Pending-shaped badge, regardless of domain

Checked by: `review`.

Icon table (`check-circle`=Pass, `xmark-circle`=Fail, `timer`=Pending, `pause`=Queued/Paused, `prohibition`=Rejected, `warning-circle`=Expired/Error) applies to any domain (billing, connectors, integrations, pipelines). Only for variants that accept `icon` (not `status` variant, which has `icon: never`).

### SBD-018 — Outside success/warning/danger, status-like badges default to neutral — info/merged/risk stay valid only as named, non-execution exceptions

Checked by: `review`.

For Pass/Fail/Pending-shaped badges, use only `success`, `warning`, `danger` for semantic meaning. Otherwise default to `muted` theme + `outline` variant. `info`/`merged`/`risk` valid only for named, non-execution exceptions (e.g., "Merged" PR badge).

## Correct

```tsx
<StatusBadge variant="status" theme="success" pulse>Live</StatusBadge>
<StatusBadge variant="outline" theme="danger" size="sm">Failed</StatusBadge>
<div aria-live="polite"><StatusBadge variant="status" theme="info">Reconnecting</StatusBadge></div>
```

## Incorrect

```tsx
<StatusBadge variant="status" icon="check">Done</StatusBadge>
```

Violates SBD-007.

```tsx
<StatusBadge variant="outline" theme="muted">Pro</StatusBadge>
```

Violates SBD-001, SBD-003.

```tsx
<StatusBadge variant="outline" theme="danger">Error</StatusBadge><StatusBadge variant="outline" theme="warning">Pending</StatusBadge>
```

Violates SBD-005.

## Known gaps

Figma, code and docs disagree here. Check the cited source before copying this behavior.

- No aria-live region; live-changing statuses must be wrapped by the caller. (SBD-008)
- Docs list variant as optional with default 'primary'; StatusBadgeProps requires it. (SBD-011; source: apps/portal/src/content/docs/components/feedback/status-badge.mdx (PropsTable) vs status-badge.tsx StatusBadgeProps)
- Icon renders in a fixed DOM order with no RTL logic. (SBD-012)
- pulse applies animate-pulse with no prefers-reduced-motion guard. (SBD-013; source: status-badge.tsx indicator span; 'reduced-motion' appears only in stepper code)
- pulse has no Figma property; it is a code-only animation.
- Contract requires children (SBD-006) but StatusBadgeProps inherits an optional children from React.HTMLAttributes, so an icon-only or empty badge type-checks. (SBD-006; source: status-badge.tsx BadgeBaseProps)
- Code Connect reads 'text#1299:25' and 'icon#1293:13'. Figma reports the keys as 'textString#1299:25' and 'viewIcon#1293:13'. The manifest uses the Figma keys; status-badge.figma.ts is unchanged. (source: Figma componentPropertyDefinitions on 1293:5995 (2026-10-20) vs status-badge.figma.ts)
- Figma defines state=hover for primary, secondary and outline. Code has no hover styles for .cn-badge, and the component is non-interactive (SBD-004). (SBD-004; source: Figma 1293:5995 variants vs packages/ui/tailwind-utils-config/components/badge.ts)
- Figma md variants bind badge/sm/gap, badge/sm/px and badge/sm/py (gap 2px, px 6px, py 2px). Code md uses badge.md.* (gap 4px, px 8px, py 4px). (source: Figma boundVariables on 1293:5995 variants (2026-10-20) vs badge.ts .cn-badge and badge.json)
- Figma status variant has 0 padding. Code applies the .cn-badge md/sm padding to the status variant (only ghost resets padding). (source: Figma 1293:5995 status variants vs badge.ts '&:where(.cn-badge-ghost)')
- tokens.refs list primary-variant colors only. Code also reads set.<theme>.secondary.*, set.<theme>.outline.bg/border and text.1 (status text). (source: badge.ts createBadgeVariantStyles)
- The outline variant has no text token in the token source; code uses set.<theme>.secondary.text for outline and ghost text. (source: badge.ts lines 28-46; mode/light/default.json set.*.outline has bg, bg-hover, bg-selected, border)

### SBD-011 — Open: docs list variant as optional with a default; the type requires it

`StatusBadgeProps` makes `variant` required. The docs site PropsTable lists it as optional with default `'primary'`. At runtime, cva `defaultVariants` does set `'primary'` when an untyped caller omits `variant`, so the docs describe runtime behavior and the type describes the contract. Needs a decision on which one is intended.

### SBD-012 — Open: icon renders in a fixed DOM order with no RTL mirroring logic

Icon renders in fixed order (`{icon}{children}`). No RTL mirroring found; unconfirmed if real-world bug.

### SBD-013 — Open: pulse animation has no prefers-reduced-motion guard

`pulse` applies `animate-pulse` unconditionally. No `prefers-reduced-motion` handling exists outside the stepper component. Needs confirmation whether a global CSS rule covers it.
